A.text: Should I run through the staff-only corridor to save time?

A.speaker: S
A.text: No. Stay on the passenger route and follow airport staff instructions.

B.speaker: T
B.text: The departure screen says last call for my connection. Can you contact the gate?

B.speaker: S
B.text: I'll try to check with the gate team. Please keep your travel documents ready.

B.speaker: T
B.text: If the gate closes before I arrive, where should I go?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Go to the airline transfer desk so they can review your booking.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Will there automatically be a seat on the next flight?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Availability varies. The airline will explain the options for your situation.

quiz.question: When does the first connection board?
May the traveler use a staff-only corridor?
Where should the traveler go if the gate closes?

A.speaker: T
A.text: I missed my connection because the first flight arrived late. Can you help?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Please show your itinerary and boarding passes so I can review the booking.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Both flights are on the same reservation. Does that information help?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Yes. I will check the available arrangements for this itinerary.

A.speaker: T
A.text: What is the earliest flight you can offer me today?

A.speaker: S
A.text: There may be a flight this evening. Let me confirm whether seats are available.

B.speaker: T
B.text: If I have to wait overnight, can you explain any assistance I may receive?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Eligibility depends on your booking and the circumstances. I'll check the applicable policy.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Please also tell me what will happen to my checked suitcase.

B.speaker: S
B.text: We will confirm the baggage arrangements before you leave the desk.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Can I get the new itinerary and any instructions in writing?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Certainly. Keep these documents and check the departure screen for updates.

quiz.question: Why did the traveler miss the connection?
choices: The airport was closed all week

quiz.question: When might another flight be available?
What does the traveler request in writing?

title: Explaining the purpose of your visit

A.speaker: S
A.text: Good afternoon. What is the purpose of your visit?

A.speaker: T
A.text: I'm here for tourism. I plan to visit museums and spend a few days with friends.

A.speaker: S
A.text: How long do you intend to stay in the country?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Ten days. My return flight is booked for the eighteenth.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Are you traveling alone or with someone else?

A.speaker: T
A.text: I'm traveling with my sister, who is waiting just behind me.

B.speaker: S
B.text: What brings you here on this trip?

B.speaker: T
B.text: I'm attending a business conference. I have the invitation and event details with me.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Will you be doing any other activities during your stay?

B.speaker: T
B.text: I will also do some sightseeing after the conference ends.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Please show the supporting information for your visit.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Certainly. Here are my conference confirmation and accommodation details.

quiz.question: What is the first purpose of travel?
How long is the first stay?
What event is the second traveler attending?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Where will you be staying during your visit?

A.speaker: T
A.text: At the Harbor Hotel for the first four nights, then with a friend.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Do you have the hotel's address available?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Yes. It is on this booking confirmation, including the phone number.

A.speaker: S
A.text: What is the total length of your planned stay?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Twelve days. I can show you the rest of my itinerary if needed.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Is this your first visit to the country?

B.speaker: T
B.text: Yes. I'm staying for one week, and all my accommodation is booked.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Will you remain in one city throughout the visit?

B.speaker: T
B.text: No. I'll spend three nights in the capital and four nights near the coast.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Can you show the address for your first night's accommodation?

B.speaker: T
B.text: Of course. Here is the confirmation with the full address.

quiz.question: How many nights are initially booked at Harbor Hotel?
How long is the first total stay?
How does the second traveler divide the week?
choices: Four in the capital and three by the coast
Three nights in the capital and four by the coast
quiz.answer: Three nights in the capital and four by the coast

A.speaker: S
A.text: Do you have a return or onward ticket?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Yes. I have a return flight next Friday. Here is the confirmation.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Which city will you fly from at the end of your visit?

A.speaker: T
A.text: I'll depart from the same city where I arrived today.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Do you have an outline of the places you plan to visit?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Yes. These are my planned destinations and accommodation bookings.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Your itinerary shows an onward flight to another country. Is that correct?

B.speaker: T
B.text: Yes. I plan to continue to New Zealand after five days here.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Have you checked the entry requirements for that onward destination?

B.speaker: T
B.text: Yes. I have the relevant documents available for inspection.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Please show the date and destination on the onward booking.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Here they are. The flight leaves on the twenty-fourth for Auckland.

quiz.question: When is the first return flight?
How long is the second traveler staying before continuing?
What is the onward destination city?

A.speaker: T
A.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the last question. Could you repeat it more slowly?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Certainly. I asked whether you have visited this country before.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Yes. I visited once about three years ago for a holiday.

A.speaker: S
A.text: And how long did you stay on that previous visit?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Two weeks. I can give you the approximate dates if that would help.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Thank you. Please answer the remaining questions as accurately as you can.

B.speaker: T
B.text: I understand some English, but I'm having trouble explaining this detail.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Tell me which part you need help with, and I will explain the available assistance.

B.speaker: T
B.text: I'm not sure whether you are asking about my current address or my hotel address.

B.speaker: S
B.text: For this question, I need the address where you will stay during this visit.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Thank you for clarifying. Here is my hotel booking with the address.

B.speaker: S
B.text: That's helpful. Please wait while I review the information.

quiz.question: When was the first traveler's previous visit?
How long was that previous visit?
Which address does the second question require?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Which baggage carousel is being used for the flight from Taipei?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Check the baggage-information screen using your flight number.

A.speaker: T
A.text: It shows carousel seven, but I don't see any suitcases moving yet.

A.speaker: S
A.text: The bags may not have arrived at the belt. Please wait behind the marked line.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Should I stay here if the flight disappears from the screen?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Ask the baggage information desk if the display changes or collection seems complete.

B.speaker: T
B.text: This belt has bags from two flights. How do I avoid taking the wrong suitcase?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Check your bag carefully, including its tag or other identifying details.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Someone has a suitcase that looks exactly like mine.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Do not rely only on the color. Confirm the identifying information before leaving.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Where can I put the suitcase while I check its tag?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Move it to the side so other passengers can reach the carousel.

quiz.question: Which carousel is displayed?
Where should passengers wait?
Is the suitcase color enough to identify a bag?

title: When your bag does not arrive

A.speaker: T
A.text: The belt has stopped, and my suitcase hasn't appeared. What should I do?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Please go to the airline's baggage service desk before leaving the collection area.

A.speaker: T
A.text: I have my baggage receipt and boarding pass with me.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Good. The agent will use the tag number to check the bag's status.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Should I wait for another carousel announcement first?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Ask the agent now, and they can tell you whether more bags are expected.

B.speaker: T
B.text: The system says my bag is delayed. Can I file a report here?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Yes. Please provide your contact details and the address where you can be reached.

B.speaker: T
B.text: How will I check for updates after I leave the airport?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Keep the reference number and use the contact method printed on your report.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Does the report mean the bag has been permanently lost?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Not necessarily. It records the issue while the airline investigates the bag's location.

quiz.question: Where should the traveler go before leaving?
What helps staff trace the bag?
What should the traveler keep for updates?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Could you describe the suitcase that has not arrived?

A.speaker: T
A.text: It is a medium-sized dark blue suitcase with four wheels and a silver handle.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Does it have any stickers, ribbons, or other distinctive features?

A.speaker: T
A.text: There is a yellow ribbon on the handle and a small scratch near one wheel.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Do you have a photo of the suitcase on your phone?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Yes. I took one before checking it in, and I can show it to you.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Is the missing bag hard-sided or soft-sided?

B.speaker: T
B.text: It is hard-sided, black, and larger than a cabin suitcase.

B.speaker: S
B.text: What name is on the luggage label, if there is one?

B.speaker: T
B.text: My full name is on the label. I can provide the details privately at the desk.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Can you also tell us the brand or any identifying features?

B.speaker: T
B.text: The brand is on the front, and a red strap goes around the middle.

quiz.question: What color is the first suitcase?
What is attached to the first handle?
What goes around the second suitcase?

A.speaker: T
A.text: I collected my suitcase, and one wheel is broken. Where should I report it?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Please bring the bag to the airline baggage desk before leaving the area.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Should I take photographs of the damage now?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Yes, keep clear photos and your baggage documents for the report.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Will someone inspect the suitcase here?

A.speaker: S
A.text: The agent can record the condition and explain the next steps.

B.speaker: T
B.text: The handle is damaged, but I only noticed it after leaving the terminal.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Contact the airline promptly and check the reporting deadline for your case.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Do I need to keep the suitcase and the baggage tag?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Yes. Keep them, along with photographs and any report or receipt.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Can you promise that the airline will replace the suitcase?

B.speaker: S
B.text: The airline must assess the claim. Ask about its process and applicable terms.

quiz.question: What is broken on the first suitcase?
What should the traveler photograph?
Is replacement guaranteed in the second conversation?
choices: Only if the suitcase is black

A.speaker: T
A.text: My delayed suitcase has been located. Can it be delivered to my hotel?

A.speaker: S
A.text: We can check the delivery options. Please confirm the full hotel address.

A.speaker: T
A.text: I'm staying there only until Thursday morning. Does that affect the delivery?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Please give us that date and an alternative contact address if your plans change.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Will the driver call before arriving?

A.speaker: S
A.text: That depends on the service. We'll explain the contact and delivery arrangements.

B.speaker: T
B.text: I need to update the phone number on my baggage report.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Please give the reference number first so I can find the correct case.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Here it is. The new number includes the country code.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Thank you. Please repeat the last four digits so I can confirm them.

B.speaker: T
B.text: They are six, two, eight, one. Could you read the full number back privately?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Certainly. We'll verify the contact details before saving the update.

What does the agent request first in the second conversation?
What are the last four phone digits?

A.speaker: T
A.text: I'm unsure whether I need to declare something in my luggage. Where should I ask?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Speak to a customs officer before choosing an exit or submitting your declaration.

A.speaker: T
A.text: I have packaged food and some gifts. Should I explain exactly what they are?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Yes. Describe the items accurately and follow the current local requirements.

A.speaker: T
A.text: If I'm uncertain about an item's status, should I simply leave it off the form?

A.speaker: S
A.text: No. Ask the officer for guidance rather than guessing.

B.speaker: T
B.text: This declaration asks whether I am carrying goods for someone else.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Are any items in your bags being transported on another person's behalf?

B.speaker: T
B.text: Yes. A family member asked me to bring a sealed gift.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Explain that to the officer and provide any information you have about the contents.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Should I open the package immediately?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Wait for the officer's instructions and answer their questions truthfully.

quiz.question: Who should clarify uncertain declaration requirements?
What items does the first traveler mention?
Who asked the second traveler to carry the gift?

A.speaker: T
A.text: Where can I buy a ticket for the airport train to the city?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Follow the train signs downstairs. The ticket machines are beside the station entrance.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Does the train stop at Central Station, or do I need to change?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Check the current route map. The station staff can confirm your destination.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Can I pay with a contactless card at the machine?

A.speaker: S
A.text: The payment options are shown on the screen. Ask the staff if you need help.

B.speaker: T
B.text: I would prefer a taxi. Where is the official taxi queue?

B.speaker: S
B.text: It is outside Door Three. Follow the signs rather than unsolicited offers.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Can I show the driver my hotel address on my phone?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Yes. Confirm the destination and ask how the fare is calculated before you leave.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Is there room for two large suitcases in a standard taxi?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Ask the queue attendant to help you find a suitable vehicle.

quiz.question: Where are the train ticket machines?
Where is the official taxi queue?
Who can help find a suitable taxi?

A.speaker: T
A.text: My flight has been cancelled. Where can I discuss a replacement booking?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Please go to the airline service desk or use its official support channel.

A.speaker: T
A.text: Should I book another flight myself before speaking to the airline?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Check your available options and the applicable terms with the airline first.

A.speaker: T
A.text: I have a connection and checked baggage on the same itinerary.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Tell the agent about the full journey so they can review both flights and baggage.

B.speaker: T
B.text: You offered a flight tomorrow morning. Can you confirm the details before I accept?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Yes. It departs at seven forty-five and arrives at ten ten.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Will my seat and baggage arrangements carry over to the new booking?

B.speaker: S
B.text: We need to confirm those separately. I'll explain what is included.

B.speaker: T
B.text: Please send me the new itinerary and any assistance information in writing.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Certainly. Review the documents carefully and ask if any detail is unclear.

Are seat and baggage arrangements automatically confirmed?

A.text: Here you are. Could I have an aisle seat if one is available?

A.text: Do I go through security before walking to the B gates?

A.speaker: S
A.text: Yes. Follow the security signs, then check the departure screen for any gate updates.

B.text: The screen now says B thirty-two. Has our flight changed gates?

B.speaker: S
B.text: Yes. Please go to B thirty-two. Your boarding time is still nine ten.

B.speaker: T
B.text: My boarding pass shows Group Three. Is it my turn to board?

B.speaker: S
B.text: We are calling Group Two now. Please wait until Group Three is announced.

B.speaker: T
B.text: I understand. I'll keep my boarding pass and passport ready.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Thank you. Please leave the boarding lane clear while you wait.

A.speaker: S
A.text: What is the purpose and length of your visit?

A.speaker: T
A.text: I'm here for a holiday, and I will stay for eight days.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Where will you be staying during that time?

A.speaker: T
A.text: At the Riverside Hotel. Here is the booking confirmation with the address.

A.speaker: S
A.text: Do you have a return ticket available to show?

A.text: Yes. My flight home leaves next Saturday. Here is the confirmation.

B.text: My flight's baggage belt has stopped, but I haven't found my suitcase.

B.text: The suitcase is green, with a white strap and a small blue tag.

B.text: I'm staying at the Riverside Hotel, and I can provide the full address.

B.speaker: S
B.text: Thank you. Keep this report number, and check the contact instructions for updates.
